tagline: Sandstone, dry river traces, and the old borax workings.
intro: From the Valley of Fire Highway side, the unimproved trail crosses the Muddy Mountains into Bitter Spring Valley toward Echo Bay. Colored sandstone and abandoned borax mines give this backway its landmarks, along with traces of rivers that have long since dried up.
The trail follows Bitter Spring Wash down to Echo Bay, on the Overton Arm of Lake Mead. Allow two to four hours for its 28 miles.

moments.title: Muddy Mountains
moments.text: Coming from Valley of Fire Highway, the track crosses the northwest of the Muddy Mountains, the range that wraps the valley's north section on three sides.

moments.title: Bitter Spring Valley
moments.text: Below Muddy Peak, 5,363 feet, the arc of Bitter Ridge runs four miles across the valley and splits it into north and south sections.

practical: High-clearance vehicles are required; four-wheel drive is recommended.

sources.label: Bureau of Land Management, Nevada Byways
